learning: Iteration 1 lost the line once per trial at about 0.06 m lateral error on every track, which points to the sensor span. If line losses fall but max_error still reaches 0.06 on bends, the next step is more turn authority (wheel_track or kp). If line losses do not fall, the cause is turn authority, not sensing.
notes: Complete robot for the Builder's ±0.06 m span proposal, with the iteration 1 controller unchanged. The span is the only geometry change, so the race isolates its effect on line loss.
rationale: Iteration 1 showed one line-loss event on every trial, with max_error at 0.061 to 0.065 on all three tracks. That matches the outermost sensor's coverage edge at about 0.06 m, so the sensing span is the likely limit. The Builder's geometry widens the outer sensors to x = ±0.06 at y = 0.03 with 16 mm footprints and a 0.10 m track. I keep the controller that raced in iteration 1 (kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.15, base_speed 1.6, last_direction) so this race isolates the span change. The sensor weights stay [-2,-1,0,1,2]. The weights are in sensor-index units, so the signal scale does not change with the span, but outer sensors now see the tape sooner, so the signal reaches its ±2 limit at a larger lateral error. I expect line_loss_events to fall and max_error to stay below about 0.06 on bends. Slalom steering_oscillation may rise because the gain per unit of error is higher at the edges. I am not raising kp this iteration, because the Builder's intent is to test the span alone.
